retrieved.title: ImagePullBackOff and ErrImagePull
retrieved.text:
## Diagnosis

1. Read the event message — it usually names the exact reference and the registry error:

   ```bash
   kubectl describe pod <pod> -n <ns>
   kubectl get events -n <ns> --field-selector involvedObject.name=<pod>
   ```

2. Confirm the image the pod is actually asking for:

   ```bash
   kubectl get pod <pod> -n <ns> -o jsonpath='{range .spec.containers[*]}{.name}{" "}{.image}{"\n"}{end}'
   ```

3. If it is a private image, check that a pull Secret exists in the same namespace and is referenced on the ServiceAccount or pod:

   ```bash
   kubectl get sa default -n <ns> -o yaml
   kubectl get secret -n <ns>
   ```

4. From a node or a debug pod, try `crictl pull` / `docker pull` with the same reference to distinguish "does not exist" from "auth" and "network".

retrieved.title: OOMKilled
retrieved.text:
## Diagnosis

1. Confirm the termination reason and the current limits:

   ```bash
   kubectl describe pod <pod> -n <ns>
   kubectl get pod <pod> -n <ns> -o jsonpath='{.spec.containers[*].resources}'
   ```

2. Compare usage if metrics are available:

   ```bash
   kubectl top pod <pod> -n <ns> --containers
   ```

3. Read previous logs for allocation errors, heap dumps, or a sudden stop.
4. Check whether the node itself is under memory pressure (`kubectl describe node <node>` and look for evictions or `MemoryPressure`).

retrieved.title: CrashLoopBackOff
retrieved.text:
## Fixes

- If the command is wrong (for example a demo container that ends in `exit 1`), correct `command`/`args` or the image entrypoint so the main process stays in the foreground.
- If a config value is missing, add the env var or volume and roll the workload.
- If a dependency is down, fix that service or make startup retry instead of exiting.
- If a liveness probe is too aggressive, increase `initialDelaySeconds` / `failureThreshold` (see probe-failures).
- After a fix, roll the deployment and confirm the restart count stops climbing:

  ```bash
  kubectl rollout status deploy/<name> -n <ns>
  kubectl get pod <pod> -n <ns> --watch
  ```

retrieved.title: Memory leak (rising working set)
retrieved.text:
## Checks

```bash
kubectl top pod <pod> -n <ns>
kubectl describe pod <pod> -n <ns>
kubectl get pod <pod> -n <ns> -o jsonpath='{.spec.containers[*].resources}'
```

In Prometheus, look at `container_memory_working_set_bytes` over 5–15 minutes, not a single sample.

retrieved.title: CreateContainerError
retrieved.text:
## Symptoms

- Pod is `Waiting` with reason `CreateContainerError`.
- Events include `Failed` from the kubelet with a runtime error (device mapper, `no space left on device`, seccomp / AppArmor / SELinux denial, invalid capability, or a missing device plugin).
- The image has often already been pulled (`ImagePullBackOff` is not the current reason).
- Application logs are typically unavailable because the container never started.
